title: Family state redundancy and future distinguishability

hypotheses.claim: One opening per two-gate channel is not generally a closed Markov state.
hypotheses.contrast: Exactly equal initial openings, different m/h, identical future V/Ca; compare canonical and frozen P.
hypotheses.interpretation: An exact collision with separated futures is a scoped insufficiency witness; off-manifold pairs do not establish reachable insufficiency.

hypotheses.claim: Reachable histories also expose information lost by openings or family aggregation.
hypotheses.contrast: Nearest distinct histories under full gate, opening and aggregate-current views; common future inputs.
hypotheses.interpretation: Approximate neighbours are descriptive, not impossibility proofs without continuity constraints.

hypotheses.claim: Slow recovery exposes state directions hidden in instantaneous current.
hypotheses.contrast: Paired central finite differences at reachable canonical states across horizons and future drives; family Jacobian spectra.
hypotheses.interpretation: Local sensitivity rank and PCA are diagnostics, not global minimal-state dimensions.

hypotheses.claim: A redundancy conclusion based only on P could reflect inherited approximation error.
hypotheses.contrast: Canonical float64, canonical float32 and all three frozen P seeds on aligned inputs and initial states.
hypotheses.interpretation: Canonical evidence is primary; report disagreements with P, do not modify P or canonical reference.

scope: Isolated ionic gate operator with externally imposed V and calcium (mM), constant conductance multipliers, dt=0.1ms. The frozen P forward is used unchanged. No membrane solver, dynamic calcium feedback, synapses or multicompartment coupling is replaced or newly validated. Existing native audits are inherited, not rerun or claimed as new evidence.
decision: Diagnostic completion does not qualify P, release a compressed model, authorize a speedup claim, or prove a globally minimal state. Tasks49/50 remain separate causal encoder/model-development stages.
